context.passage:
A Better Way to Watch Whales

QUEBEC CITY (30 May)-A new local
firm, Saguenay Eco-A dventure (SEA), will

offer whale-watching tours in the
St. Lawrence River beginning in July.
Tour participants will travel in

comfortable charter buses from Quebec City
to the boat's departure point on the
St. Lawrence River.

The bus trip is a scenic drive of just
under three hours and includes a stop at
Montmorency Falls, a popular tourist site.

Half-day cruises are available on either a
large boat with a spacious deck or a small
boat offering a more intimate experience.

Although whales are the main focus,

many different types of marine mammals
and birds are also likely to be seen in the
area. Knowledgeable tour guides will
provide expert commentary and help visitors
spot wildlife.

One feature sets these tours apart. SEA
is one of the few whale-watching tour
companies that rely on renewable energy
sources. SEA's buses and boats are powered
by biodiesel, and the larger boats are
equipped with solar panels to power their
electrical equipment.

Visit saguenayecoadventure.ca for more
details.

Review of Saguenay Eco-A dventure's Whale-Watching Tour

10 July-I recently took an excursion with Saguenay Eco-A dventure (SEA).
Although it was foggy and rainy when we boarded our boat, the fog cleared after an
hour, and the visibility was excellent the rest of the day. We saw numerous whales,
seals, and other wildlife. The boat was big and roomy, and our tour guide, Pierre, was
excellent. He gave the tour in both French and English, seamlessly alternating
between the two languages. My only disappointment was the bus ride to the boat
launch site. The bus driver was instructed not to stop at Montmorency Falls because
there was unusually heavy traffic in the area, and SEA did not want us to miss our
boat departure. I wanted to see the falls, but | was thankful we arrived at the launch

site on time.

-Otto Pfeiffer
